course_name_original: Técnicas de expresión oral y escrita (14360)
prerequisites: Perfect spoken and written command of Spanish is essential. Without correct language proficiency, it will not be possible to pass the course.

learning_outcomes.text: Distinguish the characteristics of spoken and written expression.
Define a topic and adequately organize ideas.
Correctly elaborate an academic-scientific text and compose and present a discourse following a logical order, with precise and appropriate language for the situation.
Make correct use of intonation and take advantage of the expressive possibilities of non-verbal communication.
Present a topic, project, or report to a specific audience.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other sources of information.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
Function effectively both individually and as part of a team.
Use different methods to communicate effectively with the engineering community and society in general.
Recognize the need and have the ability to voluntarily develop continuous learning.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Ability to communicate knowledge orally and in writing, to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Ability to establish good interpersonal communication and to work in multidisciplinary and international teams.
Motivation and ability to engage in autonomous lifelong learning, allowing them to adapt to new situations.

syllabus_topics: Planning, design, and organization of content.
Appropriate use of language: precision, synthesis, and correction.
Effective structure of an academic-scientific text: introduction, development, and conclusion.
Correct argumentative structure and discourse coherence.
Elements of rhetoric and oratory for effective presentation.
Oral expression in specific relational situations: group presentations, participation in debates.
Organization and execution of oral presentation. Resolution of unforeseen events in a presentation.
Communication through a screen: technologies and effectiveness in communication.
teaching_methods: Practice-based activities for idea generation, prioritization, and organization
Guided exercises for text construction, vocabulary enrichment, and error detection
Analysis and commentary of various types of texts
Critical reflection by peers and the teacher

assessment_methods.method: Attendance, participation, completion/submission of proposed activities and exercises
Completion of an expository-argumentative written work

assessment_rules: This is a continuous assessment course requiring at least 85% attendance, though mere attendance does not guarantee a pass. The final grade is based on attendance, participation, activities (50%), a compulsory written work (25%), and a compulsory oral presentation (25%). Plagiarism results in automatic failure with no recovery for the current academic year. A recovery opportunity within the same semester is available for students who attended at least 50% of sessions, involving an assignment specified by the teacher.
